title: A hierarchy with a class reachable by two paths cannot be registered
text_original: Fix `include_subclasses` when used with `configure_tagged_union` and classes using diamond inheritance. Fixes #685.
text_rewritten: Our domain model uses mixin-style multiple inheritance, so one leaf class is reachable from the root through more than one intermediate class. Registering that hierarchy with the subclass strategy and asking for a discriminator tag fails with `AttributeError: type object 'Merge' has no attribute '__args__'`. The same hierarchy registers fine as soon as the multiple-inheritance leaf is removed, so the duplication is what breaks it - the leaf is apparently collected once per path through the hierarchy and the duplicate ends up somewhere that expects a union. Reaching a class twice while walking a hierarchy should just mean it is listed once. After registration, structuring against the root should pick whichever class the discriminator names, including the multiply-reachable one.

acceptance_hint: A hierarchy where a class is reachable from the root by several paths registers with the tag strategy without raising and round-trips every member through its discriminator; single-path hierarchies keep working.
